thread:
alyssa: Quick heads-up — saw a ~18% throughput drop on flash_paged vs flash_attn_v2 with interleaved KV when running bfloat16 on A100s today.

mike: ugh, when you say interleaved KV do you mean the 64B-aligned interleaved layout we shipped last month?

alyssa: yes, exact layout. repro command: `./bench_attn --model=gpt2x --kernel=flash_paged --kv-layout=interleaved --dtype=bfloat16 --batch=8 --seq=1024`

cheng: can you paste the profiler output? even a short flamegraph snip helps.

alyssa: pasted below (trimmed):
```
GPU: A100-SXM4
kernel: flash_paged_forward_v1  time=6.8ms  tokens/sec=85k  SM_util=72%  memcpy-kv=0.9ms
kernel: flash_attn_v2_forward  time=5.6ms  tokens/sec=104k SM_util=78%  memcpy-kv=0.2ms
batching: continuous batching active, avg batch size=6.7
KV-cache stride: 256 bytes, dtype=bfloat16
```

sam: memcpy-kv at 0.9ms seems suspiciously high. interleaved layout may cause more unaligned copies when page boundaries hit.

luis: Is the page-size being used the same? flash_paged expects page-aligned KV blocks; if interleaved splits a sequence across pages, we do extra memcpy and branch work.

alyssa: exactly — I instrumented page-boundary counts: interleaved has ~12% more page-splits at seq=1024 for our key layout.

mike: what about dtype? bfloat16 vs float16 — any diff?

alyssa: interestingly bfloat16 gets worse here. float16 shows only ~6% regression vs v2. hypothesis: our memcpy path assumes 2-byte alignment friendly loads; bfloat16 packing plus stride cause more unaligned loads on the hot path.

cheng: can we try a quick microbenchmark toggling stride and alignment padding? e.g., pad KV rows to 128B boundary and re-run flash_paged.

alyssa: already tried: padding to 128B reduces memcpy overhead to 0.35ms and brings tokens/sec within 3% of flash_attn_v2.

infra-bot: deploy-notes: rolling canary scheduled for kv-layout-patch at 14:00 UTC, 2 nodes.

mike: good. Also worth testing fused_attention variant — fused kernel might hide memcpy costs if it fuses KV gather with compute.

sam: on my local run fused_attention actually increased latency for small batches (batch<=4) because it disables certain continuous-batching heuristics. For larger batches it wins.

luis: so kernel selection needs to consider batch-size distribution and KV layout simultaneously. we should add a scoring function: score = latency_estimate * tail_weight + throughput_estimate * p95_weight + memcpy_penalty*alpha.

cheng: agreed. Also add dtype multiplier: bfloat16_penalty if bfloat16 and interleaved_layout true. we can collect these signals from perf telemetry.

alyssa: I'm filing a small PR: 1) add 128B alignment pad as opt-in in runtime model configs, 2) add runtime kernel fallback rule: if page-split ratio > 8% prefer flash_attn_v2 or pad layout, 3) log page-split metric to tracing.

mike: SGTM. one nit: make pad opt-in default false for now, but enable for Dedicated customers with high-seq workloads.

sam: i'll run a sweep over batch heuristics to see how often fused beats v2 vs flash_paged across seq distribution [64,256,512,1024]. will push results later.

alyssa: thanks. For the ticket, assign to eng-runtime and tag eng-ml for kernel insights. I'll attach the microbench logs in the ticket.

luis: minor follow-up — can we also test interleaved vs separate KV layout for mixed dtype (key=float16, value=bfloat16) cases? some quantized pipelines do that and it might affect alignment.

alyssa: good call, will add.

mike: thanks all. try to keep the canary small and monitor tokens/sec, p95, memcpy-ms, and page-split-count on the new dashboard panel. :eyes:

cheng: ping me if you want help wiring the panel.

alyssa: will do. :thumbsup:
